paragraphs.text: [BETA] 上下文压缩收据 for DeepSeek Harness：审计压缩丢了你哪几条要求，并（实验性）接管压缩逐字保留。实验性部分尚未经真实压缩验证。
# dsh-compact-receipt

> ## ⚠️ Beta (0.4.0-beta.1)
>
> **A default install is safe**: it records, audits and guards; it doe

s not change compaction.
>
> **The compaction takeover is experimental and has not been exercised by

a real compaction yet.**
> Two end-to-end runs never triggered compaction (likely `auto` not enable

d or a threshold floor),
> so the pinned block has never been produced in a live session - only unit

-tested.
>
> The takeover is off by default and requires both `engine: true` and disabling the `comp

action-basic`
> row. Until a real compaction verifies it, **do not use it on important sessions**.
中文 | English
> Long conversations don't forget. Nobody tells you when they started.

Context compaction in DSH is **silent and lossy**: a range of history is replaced by one summary,
an

d from then on that summary is all the model can see. The "don't touch tests/" you said 40 turns
ago
may have vanished in a compaction — with nothing to indicate it.

This plugin hands you a **receipt** after every compaction: how much was eaten, and which of your
re
quirements no longer appear in the summary.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
## Not another context dashboard
Existing tools measure **how big** the context is (`dsh-context`) or make it **smaller** (`billion-c

ontext`).
This one measures a different thing: after compaction, **are the things you asked for stil
This one measures a different thing: after compaction, **are the things you asked for still there?**

- Others optimize token count; this audits semantic fidelity
- Others ask you to pin a passage by ha

nd (`dsh-highlightpin`); this is automatic and zero-config
- The audit **never calls a model**: the

summary is a string, your requirements are strings, so the
comparison is string comparison — **zero
token cost**, cheap enough to run on every compaction
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart DSH. No configuration, no toggles.
## Usage
| Command | Purpose |

| `/contract` | Latest receipt, commitments still in force, lifetime survival rate |
| `/contract gu

ard off` | Disable blocking (on by default) |
| `/contract unblock <id>` | Lift one rule |
## Architecture (v0.3)
- **Semantic classification**: one batched call over the shadowed messages adds the phrasings the ru

les
miss ("tests 目录先别碰") to the commitment table - this is what moves coverage from rules to the mod

el.
- **Semantic judgement**: commitments plus the new summary go to the model in one call that
retu

rns kept/lost/unclear. If it cannot answer, the rule scorer runs and the receipt says so.
- **Delive

ry is verified**: an injected message echoes back as a `user/message` event; the receipt
only claims

"confirmed delivered" when that echo arrives. A successful write is not delivery.
- **Classificatio

n probe**: `/contract probe` measures what a pinned policy would keep and how much
context it would

cost, without changing anything.
- **Rule-layer accuracy is measured, not asserted**: `test/corpus.j

s` holds 21 labelled messages and
`npm test` prints the score. Today the rules reach **86%** (100% p

recision on constraints, decisions
and acceptance; 70% constraint recall) - postposed negations like

"tests 目录先别碰" are the misses,
and the semantic layer covers them.
## It also does two more things
**1. It tells you inside the conversation.** When a compaction drops requirements, a receipt card ap

pears
in the chat — visible in the Web UI without remembering any command. That card also hands the

dropped
requirements back to the model, so it is both an alert and the cheapest possible repair.
**2. It blocks contradicting writes.** Once "don't touch X" is recorded, a write-family tool call ta

rgeting
`X` is denied, with a message telling the agent to confirm with you first, or you to run
`/c

ontract unblock <id>`. Only file-writing tools are covered, and matching is path-string based:
missi
ng a block is preferable to a false block.
## What counts as a requirement
Three kinds, matched by rules (Chinese and English):
| Kind | Examples |

| constraint | don't touch X, must use Y, 不要改 X, 必须用 Y |
| decision | we'll use X, 决定采用 Y |
| accept
ance | acceptance: tests must pass, 验收标准是 X |
Extraction is deterministic: same input, same output. No cost, no network, reproducible.
## Honest limits
This plugin does not pretend to be smarter than it is:
1. **"Possibly lost" means possibly.** A summary that keeps the meaning but rewords it can trigger a

false alarm. The threshold deliberately prefers false alarms over silence.
2. **Only the compacted

range is audited.** Requirements still in context are not audited, because
they were never dropped.
3. **Rule extraction misses things.** It recognizes common imperative phrasing and nothing else. It

does not guess.
4. **It does not prevent compaction and cannot restore the original text.** It makes

the loss visible and
puts the dropped requirements back in front of the model.
5. **Blocking is pat

h-string matching.** Only file-writing tool arguments are inspected; a different spelling
of the sam

e path (symlink, relative form) can slip through.
6. **No dedicated sidebar panel.** A client plugin

needs the custom `window.__ModuleLoader__` bundle
format, `ctx.slots`, and a React build; this vers

ion does not ship one. Visibility comes from the
in-conversation card and `/contract`.
7. **It does

not take over the compactor.** Replacing `CompactionEngine` means reimplementing
summarisation, rang

e selection and checkpoint writes, reachable only from a long live session and
not verifiable offlin

e. This version guarantees at the compaction boundary (re-inject + echo
confirmation) instead of rep

lacing the engine.
8. **The card costs tokens.** It only appears when something was actually lost —

typically 4-6 lines, far
less than the loss it prevents.
## How it works
DSH writes a `compaction/summary` event carrying the summary text and the seqs of shadowed history.

The plugin subscribes to the session event stream, extracts commitments from user messages as they
a

rrive, and on compaction scores each one against the summary text: exact match for Latin
identifiers
, character-bigram overlap for Chinese, averaged. No model calls, no network, no extra tokens.
